title: ProviderShapeSessionOps
description: Request/result bodies for the provider-shape-session/* operations (spec.md §8.5): recording what a provider's own tests produced into a provider-shape document. Behind the 'provider-shape-recording' capability (spec.md §5.3). The document this session writes is design 2.8's, opaque here.

provider.description: The provider the recorded shape is about. There is no consumer: one provider shape is compared against every consumer that has a pact with it (design 2.8 §2.1).

kind.description: The transport kind whose parts are observed (ADR 0086 decision 3), unless an observation names its own: the session reads what that transport declares (component-interfaces spec §5) — which part answers an exchange, its outcome slots and its credential members. 'http' when absent. 'message', when no transport serves it, is what produce-message hooks produce (ADR 0090 decision 3): a 'message' part answering a synchronous message's 'request', with no outcome slots and no credential members. Any other kind no transport serves is component-unavailable.

RecordingPolicy.title: RecordingPolicy
RecordingPolicy.description: How the recorder decides whether a scalar position is a closed set of values or samples of an open domain. Both members are judgements a recorder cannot avoid, so they are named rather than buried; an engine that omits them uses its own documented defaults.

max-options.description: Beyond this many distinct values, the position is an open domain whatever the repetition says.

min-evidence.description: Below this many observations, 'every value was new' is not evidence of an open domain.

ObserveResponse.title: ObserveResponse
ObserveResponse.description: One answer the provider produced, as an arrival (ADR 0086 decision 3): the transport's own parts, read as a verification reads what a provider answered. The engine makes no call here and holds no opinion about how the provider was called.

kind.description: The kind whose parts these are, read as 'create''s 'kind' is, when it is not the session's (ADR 0090 decision 4): so one session records a provider's HTTP answers and its messages into one shape. A kind nothing serves is component-unavailable.

description.description: What a report calls the entry: the consumer's words when the test knows them, else the provider's own name for the operation, such as 'GET /orders/{id}' (ADR 0086 decision 1). With 'states' and 'operation', the entry's identity.

states.description: Provider state names only — a provider knows its own state vocabulary, never a given consumer's parameter values (design 2.8 §2.2).

operation.description: The operation this answers, as shapes over the slots that identify it, part name -> slot name -> shape (ADR 0086 decision 1): the initiating part's, or for an asynchronous message, which has none, the message's own, its metadata or a member of its body (ADR 0090 decision 1). It is the recorded entry's selector (design 2.8 §2.2), with the answer's outcome slots written into it as 'equality' (component-interfaces spec §5.10). Shapes are design 2.2's document, opaque here; one that is not a shape is interaction-invalid at '/operation/...'. An operation that does not admit a part it names and 'parts' carries is interaction-invalid at '/operation'.

parts.description: The transport's own parts, part name -> slot name -> the value that slot carried (ADR 0086 decision 3). The answering part is recorded, and for a kind with none every part but the initiating one; an initiating part is only checked against 'operation'. A produced message's body with no 'content-type' is read by the type a verification reads it as: its metadata's 'contentType', else what its octets are detected as (ADR 0090 decision 3). A slot the provider did not produce is left out; it is not observed, which is a different fact from a member being absent inside a value.

ObservedSlotValue.title: ObservedSlotValue
ObservedSlotValue.description: One slot's value, wrapped the way contract spec §5.3 wraps one. A content slot carries its octets, tagged 'base64', and the type they are labelled with.

content.description: The value: a plain value as the transport presents it, or a content slot's octets.

encoded.description: Representation tag for 'content' (spec.md §2.4-2.5). Absent means the natural JSON value; 'base64' means content is a string carrying the base64 of an octet sequence.

content-type.description: The type the slot's octets are labelled with: a content component that handles it decodes them, as a verification decodes a reply. Octets it cannot decode are recorded as octets, with a warning; octets no component claims are recorded as octets.

observations.description: How many responses this session has recorded in total, so a host can report progress without holding its own counters.

interactions.description: How many distinct entries those responses covered: one per description, state names and selector, the outcome included.

warnings.description: What this observation recorded other than as given, such as a body labelled with a type it did not decode as. Absent when there is nothing to say.

ShapeWrite.title: ShapeWrite
ShapeWrite.description: Have the engine's host write the shape, merged with what every other source recorded (ADR 0086 decision 7). Behind the 'contract-writing' capability; an engine without a writer answers component-unavailable naming 'contract-writer'.

path.description: Where the shape is written, absolute. Its directory is created.

evidence.description: Where the recorder's counts are kept, absolute: a file of each source's evidence, read and rewritten under its own lock, which is held until the shape is written. Not a document to publish.

source.description: Whose evidence this session's is, such as the test file: it replaces what the same source recorded before, so a test file run twice counts once.

FinaliseRecordingResult.title: FinaliseRecordingResult
FinaliseRecordingResult.description: The recorded document, and the end of the session. Always produced: unlike a consumer session's finalise, there is no honesty rule to apply, because a provider shape claims only that these responses were produced, never that a test passed. With 'write', it is the shape written, from every source's evidence, and 'written' says where.

provider-shape.description: Design 2.8's ProviderShape document, with provenance 'recorded'. Opaque here.

written.description: The path the shape was written to, when 'write' was given.
